chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He would not enter Paradise: the shedder of blood, nor the drinker of wine, nor the backbiter who goes about spreading slander.

key_terms.مَشَّاءٌ بِنَمِيمٍ: The backbiter/slanderer who goes about spreading discord

ai.seo_question: Who are the three types of people who will not enter Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights three major destructive sins—shed blood, consuming khamr, and practicing namim (slander)—as definitive barriers to Paradise. In Shia scholarship, these are often viewed as the 'roots' of social and spiritual decay, with namim specifically targeting the fabric of communal unity (ukhuwwah). The inclusion of 'shedding blood' underscores the gravity of unjust killing, a theme central to the legacy of Imam al-Husayn.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from a man, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘He would not be entering the Paradise, the one who shed the blood, nor the one who drank the wine, nor a slandering backbiter’.
